design.activation: two keys: the committed sealed policy key (source of truth for what the gate is) and the Founder decision record in the durable state (control.finalization.reviewGovernance.model == CLAUDE_ONLY). runTick (automation/lib/orchestrator-engine.mjs activateReviewGate) records control.reviewGate {active, model, required, codexRequired false, activatedBy, activatedAt, historicalCodexEvidence PRESERVED} once as a hash-chained REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED transition at the start of a tick, never while Global Stop is active. The policy key alone, the record alone or a malformed key/record activates nothing, so the earlier, stricter gate stays; this also keeps every existing selftest world that runs the committed policy (orchestrator, autonomy-hardening, executor integration, bootstrap, crash-resume) on its previous behaviour
design.scheduling: review-quorum.mjs requiredReviewers returns [claude] for every open package and release audit when control.reviewGate is a valid CLAUDE_ONLY record, regardless of DUAL/CODEX_ONLY_HISTORICAL markers; usesReviewerGate routes every package through the per-provider gate path, so the legacy Codex-only action and a Codex review action are never scheduled; the COMMITTED transition leaves markers untouched under CLAUDE_ONLY
design.quorum: computeReviewAggregate with required [claude]: Claude CLEAN -> CLEAN; Claude BLOCKED -> BLOCKED (remediation, attributed findings, cycle limit unchanged); INVALID after the format retry -> Founder decision; quota -> provider wait without cycle use. Option alsoBlocking [codex] keeps a valid Codex BLOCKED already recorded for the same frozen bundle and cycle blocking (no reviewer overrules another's valid finding); a missing, pending, quota-blocked or malformed Codex result never holds the gate. Default alsoBlocking [] is the previous behaviour
design.mergeGate: orchestrator-executors.mjs merge: when control.reviewGate is CLAUDE_ONLY and the committed policy defines it, reviewSatisfiesGate requires a recorded CLEAN with CLAUDE_REVIEWER evidence for the current bundle digest and cycle, and verifyCleanEvidence re-derives that evidence with its identity bound to the frozen bundle digest, base, reviewed commit and cycle (same binding as the dual gate). A control-state gate without the policy key falls back to the previous gates (fail closed). For an orchestrator-built revision (execution provenance) the execution merge gate checks producer != reviewer on identity, process, workspace and session order instead of on provider (claudeOnlyExecutionMergeDenial, remediation round 1); any refusal is NOT_FF EXECUTION_MERGE_GATE_DENIED_FOR_CLAUDE_REVIEWER:<reason> before any Git operation

findings.title: Under CLAUDE_ONLY no orchestrator-built or orchestrator-remediated revision can ever merge, so a Claude BLOCKED leads to a Founder decision instead of an integrated fix
findings.rootCause: merge() passed reviewerProvider ANTHROPIC to assertExecutionMergeGate (automation/lib/execution-routing.mjs), which requires registry.pipeline.independentReviewerProvider (OPENAI in config/execution-backends.json) and rejects a reviewer provider equal to the producer provider; every builder backend is ANTHROPIC and builderRound always records LOCAL_CLAUDE provenance, so Claude BLOCKED -> REMEDIATE -> Claude CLEAN -> MERGE always ended NOT_FF -> FOUNDER_DECISION_PENDING. The engine selftest hid it with a fake merge executor, and the real-executor case asserted the denial
findings.fix: automation/lib/orchestrator-executors.mjs (allowed path, no change to execution-routing.mjs or config/execution-backends.json): new exported pure function claudeOnlyExecutionMergeDenial. Under CLAUDE_ONLY, after the Claude evidence has been re-derived and bound to the frozen bundle (unchanged), the execution merge gate (1) loads the registry with all loadExecutionBackendRegistry checks, (2) validates the provenance with the exported validateExecutionProvenance (registered builder backend, session type, provider, tool, isolated non-default branch, workspace, source commit, timestamps, digests) with resultCommit = the reviewed commit, (3) requires mergeRequiresGovernedResult CLEAN and producerMayReviewOwnOutput false, (4) requires the evidence and its run manifest to name the reviewed commit, (5) requires the reviewer to be the canonical CLAUDE_REVIEWER broker process of the control plane, (6) requires the configured builder identity (config/automation.json builder.identity, CLAUDE_BUILDER) to differ from the reviewer identity and to equal the builder identity recorded in the reviewer run manifest, (7) requires the review clone to be outside the builder workspace (basename differs from provenance.workspaceId and not under controlRoot/impl), and (8) requires the review to have started at or after the builder round finished. Any failure is NOT_FF EXECUTION_MERGE_GATE_DENIED_FOR_CLAUDE_REVIEWER:<reason> with no Git operation. The provider literal is no longer used under CLAUDE_ONLY; the legacy branch (no activation) is byte-for-byte the previous assertExecutionMergeGate call
findings.whyNotWeakening: Under the Founder rule producer != reviewer is CLAUDE_BUILDER vs an independent CLAUDE_REVIEWER of the same provider, so a provider-based independence check can only be satisfied by the Codex reviewer the Founder removed. The previous check passed the literal 'OPENAI' and was not linked to any evidence; the new check is derived from the re-derived reviewer evidence and the recorded provenance, and adds workspace and session-order separation
findings.testChanges: the merge-gate scenario no longer asserts the (defective) REVIEWER_NOT_INDEPENDENT_PROVIDER denial; it now asserts five refusals (producer workspace is the review clone, review started before the producer finished, reviewer evidence naming the reviewer as the builder, producer on the default branch, provenance not matching its registry backend) and a MERGED for valid provenance with a valid governed Claude CLEAN. The new real-executor scenario drives runTick with the production executors: real IMPLEMENT builder round (LOCAL_CLAUDE provenance) -> real CLAUDE_REVIEWER review BLOCKED -> real REMEDIATE builder round with the attributed finding -> real cycle-2 CLAUDE_REVIEWER CLEAN resolving the finding with bound retest evidence -> real fast-forward merge (CLOSED, master = remediated commit); Codex is never called

findings.title: GOV1 activation cannot reach the running supervisor without a merge that Codex must approve, and the running plane is due to schedule Codex reviews again
findings.dispositionReason: The observation is about the deployment state of the running supervisor, not a defect in the GOV1 code: no change inside the 13 allowed paths can change code that is already running. The remedy (stop the running plane from scheduling Codex, e.g. Global Stop; then a Founder-authorized governed bootstrap that integrates GOV1 and its ancestors on governed CLAUDE_REVIEWER CLEAN evidence and records a control-plane switch) is a supervisor action; this builder must not touch %LOCALAPPDATA%\UASCO, .ai/cache, scheduled tasks or the live state. Within the package, the checkpoint notClaimed and docs/architecture/DUAL-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW.md now state that a control plane predating GOV1 schedules Codex reviews and that the gate is not active in the running engine until a REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED transition appears in the live transition log

findings.source: independent verification round 2 (upheld); reproduction gov1-verify/gate-probes/hold-probe.mjs in the supervisor scratchpad
findings.title: The activation never releases the CLAUDE_ONLY_GOVERNANCE_ACTIVE transition holds, so the recorded gate never reaches any open package in the real durable state
findings.rootCause: The bootstrap supervisor retired the Codex-required queue states by holding every open package of the durable state with hold {until: CLAUDE_ONLY_GOVERNANCE_ACTIVE, by: BOOTSTRAP_SUPERVISOR, previousHold, previousNotBefore} and notBefore 9999-12-31T00:00:00.000Z. nextAction skips every package with a hold or a future notBefore. activateReviewGate and its call in runTick only wrote control.reviewGate, and the only hold-release code (orchestrator-daemon.mjs releaseActivationHolds) handles DUAL_REVIEW_ACTIVE and RELEASE_AUDIT_ACTIVE only. So after REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED every held package stayed held for ever: the gate was recorded but no package could be reviewed, merged or released
findings.fix: automation/lib/orchestrator-engine.mjs (allowed path; orchestrator-daemon.mjs is outside the package and unchanged): new exported pure function releaseClaudeOnlyHolds(control, now, policy) and the exported constant CLAUDE_ONLY_HOLD. It acts only when all three keys hold: a valid recorded CLAUDE_ONLY gate (claudeOnlyGate), the committed policy key (claudeOnlyPolicy) and the Founder record (founderClaudeOnlyRecord). It selects exactly the packages with hold.until === CLAUDE_ONLY_GOVERNANCE_ACTIVE that are not CLOSED or MERGED. Per package it deletes the hold; restores notBefore to hold.previousNotBefore, or deletes it when that is null, not an ISO time or a far-future hold marker (more than 365 days after now); and records holdReleased {until, reason, releasedAt, activationRecord {transition REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED, model, activatedBy, activatedAt, founderRecord}, supersededPreviousHold, restoredPreviousHold} (an earlier holdReleased is kept as earlierHoldReleased). The status, the Founder decision fields and every other field stay unchanged, so a FOUNDER_DECISION_PENDING package keeps its decision. The change is one ACTIVATION_HOLD_RELEASED event (reason CLAUDE_ONLY_GOVERNANCE_ACTIVE:<ids>, evidence per package) that runTick commits through the same persist/commitTransition hash chain as REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED. runTick calls it inside the existing Global Stop guard, right after the activation and before the reconciliation, so on the activating tick ACTIVATION_HOLD_RELEASED is the transition directly after REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED, and on every later tick where the gate is active and such holds remain it runs again (idempotent; nothing to do means no transition)

previousHoldDecision.DUAL_REVIEW_ACTIVE: superseded: under CLAUDE_ONLY the dual-review prerequisite no longer exists, so the package is released and the earlier hold is recorded as supersededPreviousHold {..., resolution SUPERSEDED_BY_CLAUDE_ONLY_GATE}
previousHoldDecision.RELEASE_AUDIT_ACTIVE: satisfied only when the state's final release audit is active (control.releaseAuditActivation.active === true, the same condition under which the daemon releases that hold); under CLAUDE_ONLY that audit is the single governed CLAUDE_FULL_REPO_REVIEW (newAudit), so it is not a Codex-era block and the package is released with supersededPreviousHold {..., resolution SATISFIED_BY_ACTIVE_RELEASE_AUDIT}. Without an active release audit the earlier hold and its notBefore are put back (restoredPreviousHold RELEASE_AUDIT_ACTIVE), so a release package never closes a release without the final audit. In the real tick the daemon records RELEASE_AUDIT_ACTIVATED before runTick, so this case does not arise with the committed policy
previousHoldDecision.other: any other earlier hold is put back unchanged with its notBefore (fail closed, restoredPreviousHold), so this plane never lifts a hold it does not own; only the CLAUDE_ONLY layer is removed

findings.testChanges: New deterministic scenario in scripts/dual-review-selftest.mjs, pinned in tests/pkg-gov1-claude-only-review-gate.test.ts. Its fixture mirrors the live durable state of 2026-10-06: CLAUDE_ONLY holds over a DUAL_REVIEW_ACTIVE hold (DR2-like), over a RELEASE_AUDIT_ACTIVE hold (LV1-like), over nothing on REVIEW_PENDING_PROVIDER_QUOTA (Q1-like), on a Codex-only REVIEW_CLEAN with CODEX_ONLY_HISTORICAL (DR1-like), on FOUNDER_DECISION_PENDING (L1-like), with a real previousNotBefore, over an unknown earlier hold, plus a package held for another activation and a CLOSED package carrying a CLAUDE_ONLY hold; Codex is AVAILABLE throughout. It proves: (1) without the activation (policy key without the Founder record, record without the policy key) runTick changes nothing and acts on nothing, and releaseClaudeOnlyHolds returns null for a recorded gate without the record, without the policy key, for a malformed recorded gate and for no gate; (2) under Global Stop neither the activation nor the release (also with the gate already recorded) happens and nothing runs; (3) the activation releases exactly the CLAUDE_ONLY holds as one ACTIVATION_HOLD_RELEASED transition directly after REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED (prevHash chain), with the holdReleased record, superseded/restored previous holds, the restored previousNotBefore, the Founder decision kept, other fields unchanged, and the other-until and CLOSED packages byte-identical; (4) the released review packages are scheduled for REVIEW provider claude only, then reviewed by the Claude reviewer alone (4 Claude calls, 0 Codex, 0 legacy) and merged with CLAUDE_ONLY evidence, the Codex-only CLEAN kept in historicalCodexReviews; the deferred package runs after its restored notBefore; a CLAUDE_ONLY hold that appears after the activation is released on the next tick (second ACTIVATION_HOLD_RELEASED, REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED still once); (5) without an active release audit the RELEASE_AUDIT_ACTIVE hold is put back and the package is not scheduled; (6) a real daemon tick (createTick) on a live-shaped state without dualReview/releaseAuditActivation records DUAL_REVIEW_ACTIVATED, RELEASE_AUDIT_ACTIVATED, REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVATED, then ACTIVATION_HOLD_RELEASED, then Claude reviews only, and the next daemon tick verifies the hash-chained log (TICK_DONE)
